target.title: fix(browser): navigate works with CDP hostname allowlist
target.body:
Closes #100819

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with `browser.ssrfPolicy.hostnameAllowlist` configured could open a browser page but then see `navigate` fail with `browser endpoint blocked by policy` when OpenClaw reconnected to its loopback CDP control endpoint.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CDP control-plane helper now adds the selected CDP host to both exact-host policy fields when a hostname allowlist is already present. This keeps the exception scoped to the exact CDP host while preserving the original browser navigation policy object and continuing to reject non-loopback CDP endpoints that are not allowlisted.

## User Impact

Users can keep a restrictive browser hostname allowlist and still use browser `navigate` against the managed loopback CDP session. Remote or non-allowlisted CDP endpoints remain blocked by the same SSRF policy checks.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp.helpers.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp.helpers.internal.test.ts` — 47 tests passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --prompt 'Review the fix for issue #100819. Scope: browser CDP control-plane SSRF policy should add the exact CDP host to hostnameAllowlist only when that list already exists, while preserving page-navigation policy behavior and non-loopback/remote allowlist enforcement. Changed files: extensions/browser/src/browser/ssrf-policy-helpers.ts and extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp.helpers.test.ts.'` — clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
